title: Environment values
summary: env gives a job or step named environment values. A shell can read them without repeating the literal text in each command.
introduction: env gives a job or step named environment values. A shell can read them without repeating the literal text in each command. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: env gives a job or step named environment values. A shell can read them without repeating the literal text in each command.

blocks.code:
env:
  CLUB_NAME: Reading club
steps:
  - run: echo "$CLUB_NAME"
blocks.title: Environment values

blocks.text: In a Linux shell step, the variable expands to Reading club. This fragment belongs inside a job.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Change the message to another fictional club name.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Ordinary environment values in source are not a safe place for credentials.
For more detail later, use this [GitHub Actions further reading](https://docs.github.com/en/actions).
